manifest.question: Can this harness detect selection quality at all? If an oracle that drops provably-worthless units by construction cannot beat a volume-matched random control, the harness is blind and every previous selection null is uninformative rather than negative.
manifest.falsification: ORACLE must beat RANDOM at one-sided Fisher p < 0.05. If it does not, the instrument is blind: withdraw the arm/idle/position/cadence nulls as evidence of no effect and redesign backlog items 1, 2, 6, 7 before running them.
caveats: The oracle is NOT a shippable policy — it reads a label no real policy can compute. It is an upper bound and a calibration device.
Ballast can hurt by DISPLACING budget or by DISTRACTING the model. The uncapped-ballast arm separates them; distractor_reads records whether the model chased the junk.
C0 still applies: one problem (longbuild), so this measures within-problem sensitivity only.
Ballast is synthetic and lexically unlike the task. Real irrelevant context is more confusable, so this is the EASY version of selection — a null here is damning, a win here is only a ceiling.
Grading is all-or-nothing; FAIL cells are not distinguished by how close they came.
